setup.caption: One factory: the founder talks to the mayor over Discord; the mayor and the floor roles — each a session started when a build step needs it — read and write one Beads ledger, which Gas City drives as a graph of beads, restarting sessions that crash. There is no other message bus. A bead is open, claimed or closed; a bead blocked by another is not offered to any agent, and a session that dies leaves its bead open for the next one. Sessions are disposable, the work is persistent.

fleet.footer: what seven at once cost the laptop
fleet.caption: Two counts of the same run. Over three days it started 242 sub-agents — 236 inside 34 workflow launches, 6 called directly — but at any one moment at most seven were alive, and ten was never reached. Agents are short-lived, a median of forty minutes each, so a large total and a small crowd are the same picture: five or more ran together for seventeen of the seventy-two hours, and that crowd, each agent driving its own browser and GPU, is the collision the report records as a load average of 37 on eight cores.

connection.title: The Claude call for a game, before and after the cleanup. Before: a whole Claude Code session, with Claude Code's own system prompt, Gaimer's prompt pasted into the user message ahead of the request, the built-in tools on, the user's CLAUDE.md files, hooks, plugins, skills and MCP servers taking part and a transcript saved. After: one plain completion, with Gaimer's prompt as the system prompt, in a file of its own, the request alone as the user message, the built-in tools off, the user's own setup kept out and no session saved. Picking Claude started up to four login shells; now the sign-in is checked once. The time limit was 5 minutes, but the call ran on; now it is 15 minutes, and then the call is stopped
connection.head: the Claude call for a game
connection.caption: How Gaimer called Claude for a game before the cleanup and how it calls it now. The whole Claude Code session became one plain completion: Gaimer's prompt is the system prompt, the request is the whole user message, and nothing of the user's own Claude Code setup takes part.

made.title: A new game: a description typed in the box goes in one call to the provider, with Gaimer's system prompt; the answer is read as a game, saved and run in the sandboxed page. A game that fails as it starts, with an error before it is ready or in the 5 seconds after that or after the player's first input, goes back once to the provider that wrote it, with its code and its error, and the fixed game takes its place; then the game is played
made.head: a new game

changed.title: The open game: a change typed in the box goes in one call with the game and the requests it was made from; the answer is change blocks, made to the game's code, or the whole game, changed, taken as it is, and when the blocks cannot be used, the whole game is asked for once. The changed game is a new version, which runs and can go back once too; Undo change goes back one version and New game closes the game

about.title: About
about.description: Addable Labs' mission and approach: AI-native, agents do the work, one person accountable, building in the open.
about.lead: An AI-native software company from Sweden, founded by Péter Blénessy. We build apps and tools where AI is part of the product and part of how the work gets done: agents plan, implement and review, and I am accountable for every decision that matters. We share what we learn along the way — and help people and teams become as much at home with AI as we are.
about.missionText: Part of why this company exists is a question I wanted answered: what can a team of AI agents actually build, and where does the approach break? That is the Labs in the name. Some of the work here is done for customers; some is an experiment run in the open, and written up whether the result flatters the method or not.
about.missionTextSecond: I stay close to the work for a second reason: agents produce a great deal very quickly, and someone has to answer for what they produce.
about.approachHeading: How we work and what we stand for

aiNative.title: AI-native
aiNative.text: AI is part of what Addable Labs builds and part of how it builds: the products on this site were made largely with AI agents, and the company's own work is organised around them.

team.title: One person, a team of agents
team.text: I set the direction, make the decisions that matter and review the result; agents plan, implement and review the work in between. Keeping the team that small keeps the decisions close to the work.

open.title: Building in the open
open.text: The public repositories carry their own documentation and, where an experiment did not live up to its brief, an honest evaluation of what it produced. The blog records the lessons as they happen. We would rather say what did not work than make it look better than it was.
